tasks.title: Raise play_seconds to the gate's Unity timeout, or say why 900 stands
tasks.why: P2. limits.json:36 play_seconds 900 is handed straight to the Unity CLI as the whole PlayMode run's timeout (legcmd.py:126-127) and to the detached job as 960 (legcmd.py:192). gate.ps1:141 sets TestTimeout 1800 for the same kind of run, and commit f258066cd6 treats 1800 s as how long a Unity run may take. Evidence of how close 900 is: a real job of 2026-10-08 (desk 02, play-4) ran ONE filtered class, TW.Tests.HudTogglePlayTests, for 7 minutes 37 seconds of its 900 s. A leg given a broader filter, or a cold editor with a domain reload, is cut at 900 s and reads that as failed tests. Honest limit of this finding: reading cannot show a run that was actually cut; no job record I read ended on its timeout. What would settle it: one `leg play` over a whole PlayMode namespace, timed.
tasks.done_when: A test in Tools/relay/test_relay.py reads $TestTimeout out of gate.ps1 and asserts limits.json play_seconds is at least that number; it is red on play_seconds 900 and green on the new value.

tasks.title: Keep only model ids that exist in agents.json prices
tasks.why: P3. agents.json:2 says every price was looked up in Claude Code's API reference on 2026-09-25, but eight keys are not models that exist: claude-mythos-5-1 (line 9), claude-fable-5 (10), claude-opus-5-5 (11), claude-opus-4-8/4-7/4-6 (13-15), claude-sonnet-5-5 (16), claude-sonnet-4-6 (18). The live ids are claude-fable-5-1, claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5 and claude-haiku-4-5, all four priced, and this run's legs report claude-opus-5, so nothing is miscounted today. The cost is the safety net: agents.py:79-82 matches the longest key the id starts with and returns 'the file names it', so an invented row is indistinguishable from a looked-up one and suppresses the 'agents.json names no price for X: priced as its dearest model' line (agents.py:272). claude-opus-5-5 is entered at $4/$20, UNDER claude-opus-5's $5/$25, so if that id ever ships the week is counted low and no line says so.
tasks.done_when: A test asserts every key of usd_per_million_tokens is in a pinned list of model ids that exist, and that an unknown id still comes back from agents.price() as unpriced.

tasks.title: Stop the amber and red token bounds from touching
tasks.why: P3. limits.json:2-3: amber_tokens.max is 260000 and red_tokens.min is the same 260000, and red_tokens.value 300000 is already its max. A retrospective may move both (config.py:31 RETRO_TUNES). So a tuning entirely inside the bounds, amber 260000 with red at its lowest, breaks config.py:58's amber < red check; runner.py:602-606 catches it and throws the WHOLE tuning away, including the leg_minutes line that was fine, printing only 'tuning refused'. And red can never be raised, only lowered, which the retro prompt (runner.py:591) does not say. The cost is small and bounded: a retrospective's work is silently dropped, never a broken run.
tasks.done_when: A test asserts amber_tokens.max < red_tokens.min, so no pair of values inside the bounds can fail config.limits(); red on the file as it stands.
